concepts.name: How fast the hands move
concepts.description: The minute hand turns 6° a minute, the hour hand 0.5° a minute, so the minute hand gains 5.5° a minute.

concepts.name: Angle between the hands
concepts.description: Measure each hand from 12 and subtract; take the smaller of the angle and 360° minus it.

concepts.name: Overlaps, opposites and right angles
concepts.description: Work out the angle gap to close, then divide by 5.5° a minute.

concepts.name: Mirror-image times
concepts.description: The time seen in a mirror is 12:00 minus the actual time.

concepts.name: Fast and slow clocks
concepts.description: A faulty clock shows a different amount of time to the true time elapsed; compare the two rates.

formulas.title: Hand speeds
formulas.prompt: How many degrees per minute does each hand move?
formulas.formula:
Minute hand: 360° ÷ 60 = 6° per minute
Hour hand: 360° ÷ 720 = 0.5° per minute
Relative: 5.5° per minute
formulas.explanation: The minute hand goes round in 60 minutes and the hour hand in 12 hours (720 minutes).
formulas.example: In 10 minutes the minute hand moves 60°.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting that the hour hand also moves.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How far does the minute hand move in 10 minutes?

formulas.title: Angle at h : m
formulas.prompt: What is the angle between the hands at h hours and m minutes?
formulas.explanation: The hour hand is at 30h + 0.5m degrees and the minute hand at 6m degrees. Subtract.
formulas.commonMistake: Using 5m instead of 5.5m (forgetting the hour hand's drift).
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the angle between the hands at 3:30.

formulas.title: Overlaps and gaps
formulas.prompt: How do you find when the hands overlap or are at a given angle?
formulas.formula:
Time (minutes) = angle gap to close ÷ 5.5
Hands overlap every 65 5/11 minutes → 11 times in 12 hours
formulas.explanation: The minute hand gains 5.5° on the hour hand each minute. Compute the initial gap and the gap you want, then divide the difference by 5.5.
formulas.applicationPrompt: When do the hands first overlap after 4:00?

formulas.title: Mirror image
formulas.prompt: What time does a mirror show when a clock actually reads h : m?
formulas.explanation: A mirror reflects positions left to right, so a hand at angle θ appears at 360° − θ.
formulas.commonMistake: Subtracting from 12 hours but leaving the minutes unchanged.
formulas.applicationPrompt: What time does a mirror show when the clock reads 4:20?

formulas.title: Gaining and losing clocks
formulas.prompt: A clock gains or loses g minutes each hour. How do you relate its reading to the true time?
formulas.formula:
Fast clock: shows 60 + g minutes for each true hour
Slow clock: shows 60 − g minutes for each true hour
True elapsed = shown elapsed × 60 ÷ (60 ± g)
formulas.explanation: Compare how many minutes the faulty clock advances in one true hour.
formulas.example: A clock that loses 5 min/hr shows 55 min per true hour. When it shows 11 h, 660 ÷ 55 = 12 true hours have passed.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the shown time as if it were the true time.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A clock loses 5 minutes per hour. How many true hours pass while it shows 11 hours?

formulas.title: When the hands make a given angle
formulas.prompt: At what time between h and h + 1 o'clock do the hands make an angle θ?
formulas.explanation: The minute hand gains 5.5° a minute and starts 30h° behind. Both signs usually give a valid time.
formulas.example: Right angle between 4 and 5: (2/11)(120 − 90) = 5 5/11 minutes and (2/11)(120 + 90) = 38 2/11 minutes past 4.
formulas.commonMistake: Giving only one of the two times.
formulas.applicationPrompt: At what times between 7 and 8 are the hands at right angles?

formulas.title: How often the hands meet
formulas.prompt: How many times do the hands coincide, point opposite ways, or stand at right angles?
formulas.formula:
In 12 hours: coincide 11 times, opposite 11 times, at right angles 22 times
In a day: 22, 22 and 44
formulas.explanation: The minute hand laps the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours, not 12, because the hour hand moves too.
formulas.example: Between noon and midnight the hands overlap 11 times (noon counted once).
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many times are the hands of a clock at right angles in a day?

levels.title: Two Hands, Two Speeds
levels.description: Everything about clocks follows from how fast each hand turns.

blocks.title: Degrees per minute
blocks.body: The minute hand goes round (360°) in 60 minutes: 6° every minute. The hour hand takes 12 hours (720 minutes): 0.5° every minute. So the minute hand gains 5.5° on the hour hand every minute.

blocks.title: The angle formula
blocks.caption: The 5.5 accounts for the hour hand drifting as the minutes pass.

blocks.title: Catching up
blocks.body: To find when the hands overlap, or make a given angle, work out the gap to close and divide by 5.5° per minute.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 o'clock?

figure.caption: The clock at 3:00
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 3:00: the hour hand is on 3 and the minute hand is on 12.

questions.explanation: At 3:00 the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand to 3. Each hour mark is 30°, so the angle is 3 × 30° = 90°.

hints.text: How many hour marks separate 12 and 3?

questions.question: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hands of a clock at 6 o'clock?

figure.caption: The clock at 6:00
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 6:00: the hour hand is on 6 and the minute hand is on 12.

questions.explanation: At 6:00 the hands point in opposite directions, so the angle is 6 × 30° = 180°.

hints.text: 12 and 6 are opposite on the dial.

questions.question: Through how many degrees does the minute hand turn in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, which is 6° per minute. So in 10 minutes it turns 60°.

hints.text: How many degrees in a full turn, and how many minutes?

commonMistakes: Using the hour hand's 0.5° per minute (5°).

questions.question: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one minute?
questions.explanation: The hour hand makes a full turn (360°) in 12 hours = 720 minutes, so it moves 360 ÷ 720 = 0.5° per minute.

hints.text: How long does the hour hand take to go once round?

questions.question: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hands of a clock at 4 o'clock?

figure.caption: The clock at 4:00
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 4:00: the hour hand is on 4 and the minute hand is on 12.

questions.explanation: At 4:00 the hour hand is at 4 × 30° = 120° from 12, and the minute hand is at 0°. The angle is 120°.

hints.text: Count the hour marks between 12 and 4.

questions.question: What is the angle, in degrees, between the hands of a clock at 3:30?

figure.caption: The clock at 3:30
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 3:30: the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4 and the minute hand is on 6.

questions.explanation: The hour hand is at 3 × 30 + 30 × 0.5 = 105°. The minute hand is at 30 × 6 = 180°. The angle is 180 − 105 = 75°.

hints.text: The hour hand has moved past the 3.
Half an hour is 15° for the hour hand.

commonMistakes: Assuming the hour hand stays exactly on the 3 (giving 90°).

questions.question: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 8:20?

figure.caption: The clock at 8:20
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 8:20: the hour hand is between 8 and 9 and the minute hand is on 4.

questions.explanation: Hour hand: 8 × 30 + 20 × 0.5 = 250°. Minute hand: 20 × 6 = 120°. The angle is 250 − 120 = 130°.

hints.text: Where is the hour hand at 8:20?

commonMistakes: Using 240 − 120 = 120° and forgetting the hour hand's drift.

questions.question: A clock reads 4:20. What time would you see in a mirror?

figure.caption: The clock at 4:20
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 4:20: the hour hand is between 4 and 5 and the minute hand is on 4.

hints.text: Reflect: the hour hand at 4 appears where 8 would be, minus the minutes effect.

commonMistakes: Subtracting the hour from 12 but leaving the minutes.

questions.question: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock do the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation: At 4:00 the hour hand is 120° ahead. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute, so it needs 120 ÷ 5.5 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes.

hints.text: How far ahead is the hour hand at 4:00?
How fast does the minute hand catch up?

questions.question: A clock gains 3 minutes every hour. It is set right at 6 a.m. How many minutes fast is it at 6 p.m. the same day, in true time?
questions.explanation: From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. is 12 true hours, during which the clock gains 3 minutes each hour: 12 × 3 = 36 minutes.
questions.method: Total error = hours × gain per hour.

hints.text: How many hours pass between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m.?

questions.question: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a full day (24 hours)?
questions.explanation: The hands coincide 11 times in every 12 hours (not 12, since the overlap at 11 to 12 merges with the one at 12:00). In 24 hours that is 22.

hints.text: The gap between overlaps is 720/11 minutes.

questions.question: A clock loses 5 minutes every hour and is set right at 6 a.m. When the clock shows 5 p.m. (11 hours later), how many true hours have passed?
questions.explanation: The clock advances only 55 minutes for each true hour. It has advanced 11 × 60 = 660 minutes, so 660 ÷ 55 = 12 true hours have passed (the true time is 6 p.m.).
solutionSteps: It advances 55 minutes per true hour.

hints.text: How many minutes does the clock show per true hour?

commonMistakes: Using 11 hours as the true time.

questions.question: The hands of a clock are at right angles at 3:00. At what time after that are they next at right angles?

figure.caption: The clock at 3:00
figure.ariaSummary: A clock face showing 3:00: the hour hand is on 3 and the minute hand is on 12.

questions.explanation: At 3:00 the minute hand is 90° behind the hour hand. It must catch up by 90° and then get 90° ahead, a total gain of 180°. 180 ÷ 5.5 = 32 8/11 minutes, so 3:32 8/11. (3:16 4/11 is when they overlap.)
questions.method: Gain the angle you need at 5.5° per minute.

hints.text: Right angle again means the minute hand is 90° on the other side.
